Hearing it read back in your voice, the pattern is plain. The reply was built from short flat statements set side by side, three of them opened with the word "One", and most paragraphs began with a sentence whose only job was to announce the paragraph. Your rules forbid each of those by name: parataxis, the rule of three, parallel structures inside a paragraph, and paragraph pinning. The reply still passed Articulate with a score of zero, so the checker cannot see those patterns yet, and I was wrong to treat a clean result as permission to send.

What I owe you is the kind of writing a person uses across a table, where one thought leads into the next for a reason and a sentence runs as long as the thought needs. Articulate also needs detectors for what it missed tonight, because a checker that passes that reply will pass the same faults in anyone's prose. My reply would serve as a failing specimen for those tests, with your readback as the expected verdict, if you want that added to the Articulate work.
